item.title: UAE pulls $3.5B from Pakistan over Iran mediation role
item.description: Days before Pakistan helped broker a ceasefire between the United States and Iran, the United Arab Emirates demanded the repayment of a $3.5 billion deposit from Islamabad's central bank — a move that amounted to roughly 21 percent of the country's foreign exchange reserves, according to the South China Morning Post. The withdrawal, which Pakistan's foreign ministry dismissed as a "routine financial transaction," has been widely interpreted as a signal of Abu Dhabi's displeasure with Pakistan's decision to step into a high-profile diplomatic role mediating between Washington and Tehran.

item.title: U.S. Navy ships cross Strait of Hormuz without Iran's approval
item.description: Several US Navy ships crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday in a move that was not coordinated with Iranian forces, according to Axios reporter Barak Ravid, citing a US official. The transit marks the first time US naval vessels have passed through the strategic waterway without Iranian approval since the US-Iran conflict began on February 28, representing a direct challenge to Tehran's claim of control over the chokepoint.

item.title: Russia accuses Ukraine of breaking Easter truce minutes after it began
item.description:
A Ukrainian drone struck a gas station in the town of Lgov in Russia's Kursk region on Saturday, injuring three people including a child, just minutes after a 32-hour Easter ceasefire announced by President Vladimir Putin took effect, according to regional governor Alexander Khinshtein. The attack, which Khinshtein reported via the messaging platform MAX, occurred shortly after the truce began at 4:00 p.m. Moscow time (1:00 p.m. GMT) on April 11.

The incident immediately cast doubt over whether the rare pause in fighting — agreed to by both Moscow and Kyiv for Orthodox Easter — would hold, echoing a pattern from last year's Easter truce when each side accused the other of hundreds of violations.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro edges past Lula for first time in Datafolha poll
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva finds himself numerically behind Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for the first time in a Datafolha poll, with the latest survey released Saturday showing the right-wing lawmaker at 46% to Lula's 45% in a simulated second-round runoff for the October presidential election. The one-point gap falls within the poll's two-percentage-point margin of error, making it a statistical tie — but the symbolic shift marks a new chapter in what has become one of Brazil's tightest presidential races in years.

item.title: US launches mine clearance mission in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Two US Navy guided-missile destroyers transited the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday in the first such passage since the US-Iran conflict began six weeks ago, as US Central Command launched an operation to clear sea mines from one of the world's most critical oil shipping routes.

item.title: GOP lawmakers accuse EU of election meddling in Hungary
item.description: Two Republican members of Congress sent a letter to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Thursday accusing the EU of "unprecedented, undemocratic interference" in Hungary's parliamentary elections, adding a new dimension to a transatlantic dispute over the vote set for Sunday, April 12.

item.title: Altman ties Molotov cocktail attack to New Yorker expose
item.description:
Hours after a 20-year-old man threw a Molotov cocktail at his San Francisco home early Friday morning, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman published a lengthy personal blog post responding to a sweeping New Yorker investigation into his character and leadership — drawing a direct line between the article's rhetoric and the attack on his family.

"There was an incendiary article about me a few days ago," Altman wrote in the post, published April 10. "Now I am awake in the middle of the night and pissed, and thinking that I have underestimated the power of words and narratives."

item.title: U.S.-Iran peace talks begin in Pakistan as Wall Street posts best week since November
item.description: U.S. stocks posted their strongest weekly gains in months as a fragile ceasefire between Washington and Tehran eased fears of a wider conflict and sent oil prices tumbling. The S&P 500 finished the week ending April 10 up roughly 3.6%, its best performance since November, while the Nasdaq Composite surged about 4.7% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 3.6%, returning to positive territory for the year.

item.title: Rubio revokes green cards of Iran hostage crisis spokeswoman's son, family
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio has revoked the green cards of three more Iranian nationals connected to Tehran's ruling establishment, the State Department announced Saturday, expanding a crackdown on regime-linked residents that began the previous week with the detention of relatives of slain military commander Qasem Soleimani.

item.title: Artemis II crew gets hero's welcome in Houston
item.description: The four astronauts of NASA's Artemis II mission arrived at Ellington Field near Johnson Space Center on Saturday to a thunderous welcome, reuniting with their families for the first time since completing a record-breaking 10-day voyage around the Moon. The crew was greeted with cheers, a standing ovation, and embraces from NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman.

item.title: Netanyahu says Israel's Iran campaign 'not over' as U.S.-Iran talks begin in Islamabad
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared Saturday night that Israel's campaign against Iran "is not over," issuing a video statement that touted what he called "historic achievements" while acknowledging that "we still have more to do," even as U.S. and Iranian negotiators held their first round of ceasefire talks in Islamabad.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV decries 'delusion of omnipotence' fueling Iran war
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV delivered his sharpest condemnation yet of the U.S.-Israel war in Iran on Saturday, presiding over an evening prayer vigil at St. Peter's Basilica where he denounced the "delusion of omnipotence" driving the conflict and demanded world leaders choose negotiation over military force.

The vigil, which featured Scripture readings and meditative recitation of Rosary prayers, coincided with the start of historic face-to-face peace talks between the United States and Iran in Islamabad, Pakistan — the first direct dialogue between Washington and Tehran since the 1979 Islamic Revolution.

item.title: Netanyahu says Iran has no functioning enrichment facilities left
item.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared on Saturday that the joint U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran had succeeded in "crushing" the Islamic republic's nuclear and ballistic missile programs, even as he insisted the war was far from over.

In a televised statement delivered as Iranian and American officials held a second round of face-to-face peace talks in Islamabad, Pakistan, Netanyahu claimed "enormous achievements" while warning that Israel reserves the right to resume hostilities at any time.

item.title: Trump says 'we win' regardless of Iran talks outcome
item.description:
President Donald Trump declared Saturday that the outcome of historic peace talks with Iran is of no consequence to the United States, telling reporters outside the White House that "whether we make a deal or not makes no difference to me" because "regardless of what happens, we win."

His remarks came as Vice President JD Vance led hours of negotiations with Iranian officials in Islamabad, Pakistan — the first direct high-level talks between Washington and Tehran since the 1979 Islamic Revolution.

item.title: Lebanon death toll passes 2,000 as Israel-Hezbollah fighting intensifies
item.description:
Lebanon's Health Ministry confirmed Saturday that at least 2,020 people have been killed and 6,436 wounded since the country was drawn into the broader U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran on March 2, as Israeli forces showed no signs of halting operations against Hezbollah despite ongoing ceasefire negotiations between Washington and Tehran.

The grim milestone came as the Israel Defense Forces reported striking approximately 200 Hezbollah targets across Lebanon overnight Friday and into Saturday, hitting what it described as terror infrastructure and rocket launchers in support of ground operations in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah, meanwhile, continued to fire rockets and drones into northern Israel, with sirens sounding across the Galilee region and a rocket striking the city of Safed on Thursday, injuring several people.

item.title: Qatar resumes full maritime navigation Sunday amid Gulf ceasefire
item.description: Qatar's Ministry of Transport announced on Friday the full resumption of maritime navigation for all types of vessels and ships beginning Sunday, April 12, 2026, marking a return to broader normalcy after weeks of restrictions tied to the regional military crisis.

item.title: US-Iran talks collapse after 21 hours with no deal, Vance says
item.description:
Vice President JD Vance announced early Sunday that marathon negotiations between the United States and Iran ended without a peace agreement after 21 hours of talks in Islamabad, Pakistan, with Tehran refusing to accept American demands on nuclear non-proliferation. Vance said Washington had been "quite flexible" but did not receive an "affirmative commitment" from Iran on abandoning its nuclear ambitions.

The breakdown came after the highest-level face-to-face engagement between American and Iranian leaders since the 1979 Islamic Revolution. Vance led the U.S. delegation alongside special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump's son-in-law, while Iran's delegation was headed by parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. Pakistan mediated the trilateral discussions, which began Saturday afternoon local time and stretched past dawn Sunday.

item.title: Trump warns China of 'big problems' over Iran arms
item.description: President Trump warned on Saturday that China would face "big problems" if it supplies weapons to Iran, sharpening the economic and geopolitical standoff between Washington and Beijing even as the two nations navigate fragile ceasefire negotiations in the Middle East. The remarks, made to reporters as he departed the White House, came days after Trump threatened a blanket 50 percent tariff on imports from any country found arming Tehran.

item.title: UK shelves Chagos Islands handover after Trump opposition
item.description:
The United Kingdom announced on Saturday that it has put on hold its plan to transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius, acknowledging that the deal cannot proceed without the backing of the United States, which President Donald Trump has withheld.

The bill underpinning the agreement has been pulled from the upcoming King's Speech, where the government's legislative agenda for the next parliamentary session will be set out in May, according to Sky News. The legislation had been working its way through Parliament but ran out of time, and officials confirmed it will not be reintroduced in the next session.

item.title: China unveils 10 incentives for Taiwan after historic Xi-Cheng meeting
item.description: China on Sunday announced a package of 10 policy measures aimed at boosting cross-strait exchanges with Taiwan, capping a historic visit by Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun that included the first meeting between leaders of the KMT and the Chinese Communist Party in nearly a decade.
